LESSON: LANGUAGE USE 5.3.1 SINGULAR AND PLURALS OF IRREGULAR NOUNS

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade three
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 5
Topic 5.3: Language Use 5.3.1 Singular and plurals of irregular nouns
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Language Use 5.3.1 Singular and plurals of irregular nouns, part of Strand 5 in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade three ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: How do we refer to things that are more than one?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Language Use 5.3.1 Singular and plurals of irregular nouns together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and collaboration: The learner’s ability to speak engagingly is enhanced as they construct correct sentences using singular and

plurals of irregular nouns.

Values:
Unity: Cooperation is enhanced as the learner collaborates with peers in group activities.

41

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Life skills (Self-esteem): The learner’s self-esteem is enhanced as they improve in the use plural forms of irregular nouns.

Links to other Learning Areas:
The learner is able to apply knowledge learnt on plurals of irregular nouns in learning of similar concept in Kiswahili Language Activities.

Suggested Learning Resources

● Print textbooks in appropriate font size and colour contrast

● Braille books

● Digital devices with assistive technology,

● Charts, flash cards or braille cards,

● Pictures or picture description
